title: Arrow-Key Explorer
body:
Goal: use events (key presses) to move a sprite with the arrow keys. Tool: Scratch app (offline). Work in pairs: the navigator predicts before each test.

Build steps

  1. Start a new project: File > New. Keep the cat or choose any sprite.
  2. From Events, drag four when (space) key pressed blocks into the code area.
  3. Click each dropdown and choose right arrow, left arrow, up arrow, down arrow.
  4. Under each one, snap one Motion block (see below).
  5. Click the stage once (so Scratch listens to the keyboard), then press the arrow keys.
  6. Save as explorer. You will use it again in Exercise 3.3.

The scripts in words

Four separate scripts on the same sprite:

  • when right arrow key pressed: change x by 10
  • when left arrow key pressed: change x by -10
  • when up arrow key pressed: change y by 10
  • when down arrow key pressed: change y by -10

(x is left and right; y is up and down.)

Expected behavior

Each arrow key moves the sprite 10 steps in that direction. Holding a key down keeps the sprite moving. No green flag is needed: each key is its own "doorbell".

Checklist

hints.label: Hint 1
hints.title: Where to look
hints.html: Look in the Events category for blocks that wait for a key. Each key is like its own doorbell. You need four separate scripts, one for each arrow key.

hints.label: Hint 2
hints.title: Try this
hints.html: Drag out four when ( ) key pressed blocks and pick a different arrow in each dropdown. Under each one, snap one block from the Motion category. Remember that x is left and right, and y is up and down.

hints.label: Hint 3
hints.title: Almost there
hints.html: Use change x by ( ) for the left and right keys, and change y by ( ) for the up and down keys. Moving right or up needs a positive number. Moving left or down needs a negative number. Click the stage once, then try the keys.
